An update to n2den, the experimental Nintendo Switch 2 recompulator built on Eden.

n2den runs decrypted dumps of games you own. It contains no decryption code, does not use console keys, and includes no games.

## Downloads

| Package | What it is |
|---|---|
| `n2Den-v1.0.3-windows-x64-pgo.zip` | **Recommended.** Built with clang, ThinLTO and a profile trained on gameplay: the faster build. The command-line `n2Den-cli.exe` is only in the MSVC package. |
| `n2Den-v1.0.3-windows-x64.zip` | The same source built with MSVC, like the test builds. Use it if the PGO build misbehaves on your machine. |
| `*-symbols.zip` | Debug symbols for crash reports. Not needed to play. |

Windows x64 with a Vulkan GPU. Extract into a new folder; create an empty `user` folder beside `n2Den.exe` for portable mode. You can extract over 1.0.1 or keep both side by side.

## What's new since 1.0.1

### New games

- **Xenoblade Chronicles 2 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition** is now in-game on NVN-HLE at full speed, with a correct picture, sound and controls.
- **Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition** is now in-game on NVN-HLE at full speed, with a correct picture and its own DLSS upscaling running as on the console.

### Graphics

- The game's own upscaling now works as on the console: its DLSS step runs on NVIDIA DLSS, followed by its own upscaling network to 4K. Before, the final 4K upscale could be missing and leave a black background.
- Fixed a fine dot pattern over the whole picture when a game's own upscaling network runs.
- Fixed blocky bright reflections under roofs and in covered areas, most visible in the rain.
- Fixed stretched triangles and flickering geometry in shadows.
- Fixed garbled menus and text in Xenoblade Chronicles 2 and Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition.
- DLSS no longer restarts every time a game changes its render resolution on the fly, so the picture stays steadier.
- Fixed a grid pattern when the Resolution setting is above 1X in games that sample half-size effects (a further, fainter one remains, see Known issues).

### Memory

- Textures that have not been used for a while are released when video memory runs low, so long sessions no longer run out of video memory.

### Options

- Every game's page now has an **Upscaling** tab that shows only the options that work for that game. The Upscaler, DLSS quality and Display resolution options moved there from the Graphics settings; the DLSS files status and download stay in Graphics.
- The NVN-HLE upscaler has a new **Console native** choice: the game's own upscaling, exactly as on the console. It is the default.
- New **Display resolution** option (Auto, 1080p, 1440p, 4K) for the games that ask what display they are connected to.
- **DLSS quality** now also works in Fast Fusion (new, not yet widely tested).
- The status bar shows which upscaling steps actually ran, for example "DLSS Quality -> Game network".
- The Ocarina of Time Dynamic FPS and Max resolution options and the Donkey Kong Bananza vsync option moved to those games' Add-Ons list.
- "Configure Current Game" now reads "Configure Selected Game..." when no game is running, and opens the selected game's settings.

| Game | Emulated GPU | NVN-HLE (Vulkan) |
|---|---|---|
| The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2) | In-game | In-game |

| Fast Fusion | Playable | Playable |
| Kirby and the Forgotten Land – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World | Playable | Playable |
| Donkey Kong Bananza | In-game | In-game |
| Orbitals Deluxe Edition | Not usable | In-game, slow |
| Xenoblade Chronicles 2 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition | Not tested | In-game |
| Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition | Not tested | In-game |

Details and known issues per game: [docs/GameProgress.md](https://github.com/Duck912/n2den/blob/main/docs/GameProgress.md). Games not in the table have not been tested.

## Known issues

- Expect missing graphics and crashes: this is a development release.
- The first start of each game after updating is slower and stutters for a while: the shader cache is rebuilt once.
- In Xenoblade Chronicles 2 a fine grid shows over the picture when the Resolution setting is above 1X; keep it at 1X. The game also uses a lot of video memory.
- Games in large `.nup` containers take a while to load because their data is unpacked at every start.
- Mario Kart World can run out of system RAM after several minutes and is not recommended for play.
- Only Windows is supported for now.

## Reporting problems

Open an issue with `user\log\eden_log.txt` (or `%APPDATA%\eden\log\eden_log.txt`), taken right after the problem, plus your GPU and driver version.
